steps.body: Recipes scale by whole numbers all the time: five batches of a 3/4-cup ingredient needs 15/4 cups, or 3 3/4.
steps.narration: Recipes scale by whole numbers all the time: five batches of a 3/4-cup ingredient needs 15/4 cups, or 3 3/4.

widget.prompt: Four batches each use 3/4 cup. Build the total cups.
widget.successFeedback: 12/4 — twelve fourths, which is exactly three cups.
widget.lowFeedback: Your bar represents less than the target value. Increase it until the values match.
widget.highFeedback: Your bar represents more than the target value. Decrease it until the values match.

commonFractions.feedback: 3/4 is one batch. Four were made.
That added the batch count to the numerator instead of taking four groups.

predict.prompt: Five batches of 3/4 cup each. Total?
predict.reveal: Five groups of three fourths collects fifteen fourths — three and three-quarter cups; adding the counts to get 8/4 would answer a different question.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x recipe.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x recipe a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: 5 identical recipes each use 7/8 cup of flour. Express the total as ?/8. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: That is ONE recipe's flour; 5 recipes each take that much.
Adding the recipe count to the numerator mixes two different things — the count multiplies.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count the equal-sized pieces first; keep the named denominator in the requested unsimplified form.

takeaways: Rename as a mixed number to measure.

concept.body: The mixed-number form is what a cook actually measures, so scaling usually ends with grouping the pieces back into wholes. The figure regroups an improper fraction into complete wholes and a remainder, the final step when a scaled recipe exceeds one cup.
concept.narration: The mixed-number form is what a cook actually measures, so scaling usually ends with grouping the pieces back into wholes. The figure regroups an improper fraction into complete wholes and a remainder, the final step when a scaled recipe exceeds one cup.

widget.prompt: Three recipes each use 5/6 cup of flour. Express the total as ?/6. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: Five sixths is one recipe; include all three recipes.
Adding the group count to the numerator does not build three equal groups.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Multiply three recipes by five sixth-sized pieces per recipe.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — the total is 15/6 cups, or 2 1/2 cups.
